name: CRR extraction benchmark - ground truth manifest
description: Indicator-level ground truth for the extraction benchmark (gap analysis §7). Each case names, per linkId, the expected value, evidence status and verbatim quote - plus the linkIds a correct extraction must NOT answer, which is where the fabrication failures actually show. This manifest is the start of the record that replaces the unreconstructable '138' figure (KI-30): every case here has named provenance, and a case with no provenance does not belong in it.

howItIsUsed.now: run-ground-truth.mjs builds each expected response, checks every quote against the note (validation-gate rule 1), and runs it through the CT CAP engine. This proves the ground truth is internally consistent and consistent with the rules BEFORE any model is involved - a benchmark whose ground truth disagrees with the engine measures nothing.
howItIsUsed.slice9: The same cases are the extraction benchmark: a model's response is scored per linkId against `expected` (value, status, quote validity) and per case against `examSites`, and the engine result is checked separately. That separation is CK Jin's recommendation and the reason a single-verdict comparison cannot replace it.

scoringNotes: `expectedAbsent` is scored, not decorative: answering one of those linkIds is a false positive, and it is the failure mode KI-01 and KI-10 describe. Weight the absent set at least as heavily as the present set.

Status is scored separately from value. `weightloss.periodMonths = 2` labelled `documented` rather than `inferred` in GT-RM-RP-007 is a wrong answer even though the number is right - that mislabelling is exactly clause 14's failure.
Quote validity is scored mechanically (does the span appear in the note) and is independent of whether the value is correct.
GT-RM-RP-001-ctcap-5.5pct is SYNTHETIC and must be reported separately from the three evaluator cases; including it in an aggregate extraction score would overstate coverage of real referrals.

coverage.gaps: One exam/site (CT CAP), five cases, 14 distinct linkIds. Nothing here exercises a red flag, the ACC redirect, a paediatric case, a compound flag, or exam/site selection with a real second bundle. GT-BROWSER-001 adds the weights-based weight-loss path and the E-07/E-08 equivalences but is still CT CAP only.

findings.finding: tests/scenarios.mjs RM-MW-009-ctcap records the quote 'painless jaundice ... Liver ~2 cm below costal margin' for workup.localisingFeatures. That is two spans joined by an ellipsis and is not a verbatim span of the note, so the validation gate (rule 1) would reject it. The scenario passes today only because run-tests.mjs does not check quotes.
findings.action: The ground truth uses 'Liver ~2 cm below costal margin'. tests/scenarios.mjs is NOT changed - outside this brief's scope. Recommend either correcting the scenario's quote or adding a quote check to run-tests.mjs so scenario quotes are held to the same standard as extraction output. Owner: Gary.

findings.finding: RP-007/INT-002's note requests 'CT A/P' (CT Abdomen/Pelvis). There is no ct_ap id in the published exam/site list - CT AP exists only as an approved draft dated 27/08/26. A model given the published list cannot return the exam the referrer actually asked for; the closest published id is ct_cap, which is a different exam.
findings.action: Record only. Affects exam/site selection accuracy scoring (slice 9) and the CT AP transcription (slice 7). Owner: Gary.

findings.finding: tests/scenarios.mjs RM-RP-001-ctcap-5.5pct has no `note` field, so it could not be used as extraction ground truth as it stood. Its note has been reconstructed by substituting 5.5% for 5% in RP-001's note - the only reading consistent with the quotes the scenario already asserts.
findings.action: Recorded in that case's provenance and flagged as synthetic in scoringNotes. Owner: Gary - confirm the reconstruction is what was intended.
